evidence: bp-obligation.lisp:196-197 `(fnn-bpo-request-publish store journal work-id attempt-id)` publishes the :attempt and outcome records and takes the submit grant. Only afterwards, line 202 `(fnn-bps-open fnbs config wall wall-error)` takes the FNBS locks (fnn-bps-lock refuses `lifecycle queue is already locked`; fnn-tcl-spool-acquire refuses `spool is already owned`), and line 215 queries the route, with 229-234 `(unless route ... (return-from fnn-command-bpo-owner-request +fnn-exit-refused+))`.
fix: Open the FNBS service and resolve the route before publishing the attempt, so a carrier refusal happens before any durable record. If it can still fail afterwards, report a distinct `attempt durable, carrier not queued` class that a later pass is proven to re-queue.
reviewer: bp-obligation.lisp:196-197 publishes the attempt and outcome and takes the submit grant (fnn-bpo-request-publish, lines 175-185) before line 202 calls fnn-bps-open. That open takes the FNBS locks and can refuse while bp-node serve holds them. Checking the lock first would avoid the durable-attempt/refused split, so that ordering is a real defect. The no-route case (229-234) is documented design: the comment says "The durable attempt keeps the obligation pinned; the carrier was refused by routing". The existing-sequence lookup (fn-bpn-host-existing-sequence) suggests a re-request can reuse the attempt, so the impact is operator confusion rather than lost work.
scenario: An operator runs `bp-obligation request` while `bp-node serve` holds the same FNBS journal, or no bp-route row matches yet. The workflow journal now durably records an attempt, its outcome and a consumed submit, but no FNBS job exists, and the verb exits `refused`. `bp-service resume` has nothing to re-offer. The attempt is accepted in one journal and absent in the carrier, yet the operator is told it was refused.
title: bp-obligation request makes the attempt durable before the carrier can refuse, then exits refused
